subgoals.objective_name: To establish and maintain effective AI risk management.

subgoals.control_name: Organizational policies, processes, and procedures for mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are established, implemented, and maintained.

subgoals.goal_name: Establish organizational policies, processes, and procedures for mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks
subgoals.embedding_context: Establish organizational policies, processes, and procedures for mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks

actions.name: Operational Activity Mapping
actions.description: Operational activity mapping identifies activities of the organization and the organization's suborganizations, groups, roles, and individuals that carry out the activities and then establishes the dependencies of the activities on the systems and people that perform those activities.
actions.reason: Operational Activity Mapping directly supports mapping AI risks by identifying organizational activities and their dependencies, which is foundational for establishing policies.

actions.name: Operational Dependency Mapping
actions.description: Operational dependency mapping identifies and models the dependencies of the organization's activities on each other and on the organization's performers (people, systems, and services.)  This may include modeling the higher- and lower-level activities of an organization forming a hierarchy, or layering, of the dependencies in an organization's activities.
actions.reason: Operational Dependency Mapping models dependencies between activities and systems, enabling structured risk assessment and management of AI-related interdependencies.

actions.name: Operational Risk Assessment
actions.description: Operational risk assessment identifies and models the vulnerabilities of, and risks to, an organization's activities individually and as a whole.
actions.reason: Operational Risk Assessment explicitly measures organizational risks, aligning with the goal of quantifying AI risks across activities.

actions.name: System Vulnerability Assessment
actions.description: System vulnerability assessment relates all the vulnerabilities of a system's components in the context of their configuration and internal dependencies and can also include assessing risk emerging from the system's design as a whole, not just the sum of individual component vulnerabilities.
actions.reason: System Vulnerability Assessment evaluates design and configuration risks in systems, contributing to measuring AI risks at the technical level.

actions.name: Validate ML Model
actions.description: Validate that machine learning models perform as intended by testing for backdoor triggers or adversarial bias. Monitor model for concept drift and training data drift, which may indicate data tampering and poisoning.
actions.reason: Validating ML models ensures they perform as intended, directly supporting risk management by detecting adversarial biases and concept drift in AI systems.

actions.name: Limit Release of Public Information
actions.description: Limit the public release of technical information about the machine learning stack used in an organization's products or services. Technical knowledge of how machine learning is used can be leveraged by adversaries to perform targeting and tailor attacks to the target system. Additionally, consider limiting the release of organizational information - including physical locations, researcher names, and department structures - from which technical details such as machine learning techniques, model architectures, or datasets may be inferred.
actions.reason: Limiting public release of technical information mitigates risks from adversarial exploitation of AI systems, aligning with policy-based risk management.

actions.name: Vulnerability Scanning
actions.description:
Vulnerability scanning is used to find potentially exploitable software vulnerabilities to remediate them.
File formats such as pickle files that are commonly used to store machine learning models can contain exploits that allow for arbitrary code execution. Both model artifacts and downstream products produced by models should be scanned for known vulnerabilities.
actions.reason: Vulnerability scanning mitigates AI risks by identifying exploitable vulnerabilities in model artifacts and downstream products.

actions.name: Access Modeling
actions.description: Access modeling captures and records the access permissions granted to identities (e.g., administrators, users, groups, systems) and optionally includes details on how these identities are stored, managed, and shared across systems.
actions.reason: Access modeling directly supports accountability by recording and mapping access permissions, ensuring traceability of who interacts with AI systems.

actions.name: Control Access to ML Models and Data in Production
actions.description: Require users to verify their identities before accessing a production model. Require authentication for API endpoints and monitor production model queries to ensure compliance with usage policies and to prevent model misuse.
actions.reason: Controlling access to ML models via authentication ensures accountability by tying actions to verified identities and enforcing usage policies.

actions.name: Monitoring and auditing
actions.description: Regularly monitoring and auditing the model’s use can help detect and prevent theft by detecting when an attacker is attempting to access or steal the model.
actions.reason: Monitoring and auditing model usage provides transparency by tracking how AI systems are applied and detecting unauthorized access or misuse.

actions.name: Human Approval
actions.description: Require user consent for privileged actions.
actions.reason: Human approval for privileged actions ensures accountability by requiring explicit consent, making decision-making processes traceable.

actions.name: Verify the authenticity of feedback data
actions.description: Use techniques such as digital signatures and checksums to verify that the feedback data received by the system is genuine, and reject any data that does not match the expected format.
actions.reason: Verifying feedback data authenticity ensures transparency by confirming the integrity of inputs, preventing AI systems from acting on compromised data.
